UCC28070 · TI Controller 65 kHz
More views · click to enlarge
Bridgeless Interleaved AC-DC PFC Boost Converter
300 W (+10% margin) converter with dual-phase interleaved boost stages using TI's UCC28070 controller. Bridgeless topology eliminates one diode forward drop per half-cycle (~0.7 V saved). Average Current Mode Control with outer voltage PI loop and inner sinusoidal current reference generated by multiplying the voltage loop output by scaled [Vg]. All component values calculated from first principles per the UCC28070 datasheet — boost L = 3.5 mH from 20% ripple target, R-RT = 34.8 kΩ for 65 kHz, Type-II compensator with zero at 18 kHz and pole at 120 kHz, 1 µF soft-start cap → 80 ms ramp. Validated in both MATLAB / Simulink (with full ACMC control loop) and LTspice (with actual UCC28070 SPICE netlist).

Simulink · Standalone Microgrid PV + BAT
PV System with Battery Storage & Bidirectional DC-DC Converter
Complete standalone renewable energy system integrating a PV array, MPPT-controlled boost converter, bidirectional DC-DC converter (buck mode for charging, boost mode for discharging), and battery bank. Incremental Conductance MPPT (operating on dI/dV = -I/V at the maximum power point) refined with a Fuzzy Logic Controller that takes error and Δerror as inputs and reduces MPP oscillation under rapidly changing irradiance. Battery control logic is a PI-regulated loop with V_ref = 24 V that monitors SOC, load demand, and PV availability to prevent over-charge and deep discharge. Result: load voltage regulated at ~24 V and load power held ~50 W despite source-side fluctuations.

Course · Power Systems HESS · FLC
More views · click to enlarge
Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) for Grid Integration
Coordinated fuel-cell + battery + supercapacitor HESS managed by a Fuzzy Logic Controller. Fuel cells respond slowly, batteries handle long-term backup, and supercapacitors absorb sudden load steps. The FLC replaces a conventional PI controller and routes power between the three sources based on load conditions, DC-bus voltage, and battery SOC. Tested in MATLAB / Simulink under load variation and fuel-cell power variation cases. Result: reduced DC-bus voltage transient magnitude vs. battery-only baseline, less battery degradation from fewer charge/discharge cycles, and smoother power transitions. Applications: off-grid power, EV charging stations, smart-home / smart-grid systems.

Undergraduate · BVRIT EV · BMS
EV BMS — Charge Monitoring & Fire Protection
Built a complete hardware prototype of a Battery Management System for electric vehicles, integrating real-time charge monitoring and a thermal fire-protection mechanism. Voltage, current, and temperature sensing throughout the pack optimizes performance and longevity; an early-warning thermal sensor system detects overheating to prevent thermal runaway; real-time data logging supports predictive maintenance and remote safety monitoring. The board (shown left) combines the BMS controller, cooling fan, heat sinks, LCD telemetry display, and a DC motor load for end-to-end demo. Project undertaken at BV Raju Institute of Technology (BVRIT) during undergraduate engineering studies.
